findings.finding: The new command `claude mcp add-json rebar '<json>'` relies on POSIX single-quote semantics to pass a JSON blob with embedded double quotes and a literal `${...}`. Two Windows shells break this. cmd.exe does not treat `'` as a quoting character, so the JSON is split at spaces with stray quote characters. Windows PowerShell 5.1 strips embedded double quotes when passing arguments to native executables.

findings.finding: The replacement Claude command `claude mcp add-json rebar '<json>'` has no scope flag. Claude Code's `mcp add`/`add-json` default to the `local` scope: a per-project entry in ~/.claude.json that applies only to the current directory, not a user-level entry. The doc presents the command as the way to set up the "user-level fallback" (~/.claude.json). Run inside this checkout, the default local scope would instead create a private entry that outranks the committed project `.mcp.json` entry. The plan does not check the add-json flag surface (`--scope`/`-s` local|project|user) against `claude mcp add-json --help`.
findings.location: Approach → Claude Code bullet; docs/mcp-client-setup.md §Claude Code (lines 166-175)
scenarios: A user follows the doc in the repo checkout. The entry lands in local scope for this directory and shadows the project `.mcp.json`, so it never acts as a user-level fallback in other directories.
A user runs it from their home directory, expecting a global entry, and finds `rebar` missing elsewhere.
